scope: Static frozen code and read-only receipt, byte-hash and progress-count audit; no recomputation or live monitoring.
checks: Pre-execution commit, registration, freeze, privacy revision and source identities match; old and intermediate freeze hashes remain preserved.
Both historical archive byte hashes and schema identities match; worker reports one numeric decoding snapshot per archive while ready/verify may stream-hash repeatedly.
Frozen trainer checks the private registered device name and kind against the actual JAX GPU and checks device placement and synchronization on each update.
The fit receipt reports 128 synchronized, nonzero-gradient updates, changed parameters and 16-group CPU/GPU comparison; progress sequence counts are consistent with the receipt.
Windows transport and Linux guard report clean process cleanup; no worker, seal or cancel failure markers exist.
The final seal binds fit, transport, guard and private checkpoint SHA; protected old model and default Bot byte hashes match.
limitations: No checkpoint or training array was decoded and no gradients, per-step device placements or logits were independently recomputed; no execution was live monitored.
Progress records and cleanup are worker and supervisor evidence, not independent continuous observation; same-user adversarial tampering is outside the guarantee.
The fixed sixteen comparison groups are from the beginning of the old dataset and do not establish parity for every new class.
GPU and host memory thresholds are sampled or software bounded, not hard memory caps; specific preflight measurements were not independently retained.
Biased teacher examples and width-filtered batches do not establish generalization, competitive improvement, automatic promotion or an independent test result.
Raw progress, replay, model arrays and private configuration remain local; only hashes and aggregates are publishable.
